clue.text: Veterans formed square

parts.note: veterans are old hands, so the word gives old
to fashion something is to form or shape it

explanation.surface: Former soldiers lined up in a square formation on the parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Square in its slang sense means conventional and out of date, a synonym for behind the times.

clue.text: Nothing odd about order book tycoon presented over part of year

indicators.note: over says the kept letters are turned round and read backwards
nothing odd means the odd-placed letters are discarded, keeping the even ones of the three words

explanation.surface: A tycoon's order book shows nothing odd when presented at the year's end.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'order book tycoon' are REBOTCO; 'presented over' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the tenth month, one portion of the calendar year.

clue.text: Crossing East, old spy changes stations

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the rearranged letters span the compass point
changes says the letters of old spy are reordered

explanation.surface: An old spy crosses into the East and switches railway stations to shake off a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges OLD SPY round E; 'stations' is a verb, positions troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To station troops is to post them in position, and to deploy them is the same action.

clue.text: Stubborn and industrious types securing first and second

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the two creatures enclose the ordinal

parts.note: the ass is proverbially stubborn
the ant is proverbially industrious; one is taken here
1ST, written as IST, is first

explanation.surface: Stubborn and hard-working people grab both first and second place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the definition, as a noun: a helper in a duel or boxing bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a supporting aide, as a boxer's or duellist's helper, so a deputy.

clue.text: Had a dream — was skipping half-heartedly

indicators.note: half the heart goes: of the doubled middle letters, one is dropped

parts.note: skipping and hopping are both springy movements

explanation.surface: Someone had a dream in which they were skipping about without enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a dream in the sense of an aspiration means wishing for something.

clue.text: Stood up to work, then sat

indicators.note: then sets the second piece after the first

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone stood to work, then sat down.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing up to someone is resisting them, a synonym for being against.

clue.text: Deterioration rising, no one angry

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sore means angry or resentful

explanation.surface: Things are getting worse, yet nobody is cross about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual wearing away, as of rock by water, is a kind of deterioration.

clue.text: Relative sending a postcard?

definitions.meaning: the adjective, meaning matching or proportionate
writing to someone by post, keeping up letters

explanation.surface: A family member sends a holiday postcard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like a family member, but it is the adjective: matching.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both matching or analogous and exchanging letters with someone, as postcard senders do.

clue.text: Considerate but grasping

explanation.surface: Someone is kind but greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' suggests greed, but here it means getting the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both sympathetic to others and comprehending an idea.

clue.text: Well-armed character that squirms when caught

definitions.text: Well-armed character that squirms when caught

parts.words: Well-armed character that squirms when caught
parts.note: the 'arms' are eight tentacles, and a sea creature landed by a fisherman writhes; well-armed suggests a heavily armed fighter

explanation.surface: A heavily armed villain wriggles when the police finally catch him.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-limbed mollusc is quite literally well supplied with arms, and it writhes when hauled from the sea.

clue.text: Music, hackneyed stuff that's supposed to enhance a film

definitions.text: that's supposed to enhance a film

parts.note: pop is popular music
corn is trite, sentimental material

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a film's trite pop soundtrack added to boost it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinemagoers munch a tub of this puffed snack because it supposedly adds to the movie-going experience.

clue.text: Bands that bring things to a close with a bow?

definitions.meaning: strips of material, as worn in the hair

definitions.text: that bring things to a close with a bow?
definitions.meaning: strips of satin tied in a bow finish off a wrapped present

explanation.surface: Musical groups end every show by bowing to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow strips of fabric are bands, and they are tied into a decorative knot to finish wrapping a gift.

clue.text: Undeterred by discharge in river

indicators.note: in places the discharge within the river's name, splitting it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to spit is to discharge saliva

explanation.surface: Someone presses on, not put off by pollution pumped into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in spite of, a preposition introducing something that fails to stop an action.

clue.text: More than one kind empress or tsarina's captured

indicators.note: captured says the letters are held within the run of words empress or tsarina's

explanation.surface: Royal women of more than one sort were taken prisoner, an empress or a tsarina.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinds and types are plural synonyms, so more than one kind is several varieties.

clue.text: Distance when flying to check carbon disasters

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so the shuffled letters surround the carbon
flying suggests the letters of distance are sent scattering into a new order

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Measuring how far a plane flies in order to monitor carbon emissions leads to disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when flying' rearranges DISTANCE to ACIDENTS, and 'to check' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidents and disasters are both unplanned mishaps causing harm, so they are near-synonyms.

clue.text: In which we learn about young woman going to space

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
a lass is a young woman
room means space

explanation.surface: We hear about a young woman heading off into outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons are taught in a school's teaching room, where pupils learn.

clue.text: Musical group or artist's carrying case

indicators.note: carrying lets the artist come along behind the case, attached to it in the order needed

parts.note: a chest is a case or box for storage
RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A band, or perhaps a painter's portable box: the setter offers two pictures of something carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ensemble of instrumentalists playing together is exactly a musical group.

clue.text: Unsettled, since he is from a far country

indicators.note: unsettled says the letters of since he are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone feels unsettled because he has come from a distant land.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes someone or something native to a distant East Asian nation.

clue.text: They are 5 twisted men, involved in scuffling I see

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the twisted men go inside
scuffling suggests the letters of I see are jostled about
twisted says the letters of men are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Five men, twisted and brawling, are seen in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to 5-down, OPPOSED. 'twisted' makes NEM; 'scuffling' makes EIES; 'involved in' puts NEM inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Foes are people who stand opposed to someone, so they are adversaries.

clue.text: Place I mentioned in communications

definitions.meaning: a country is a place on the map
radio operators spell out letters with code words, and the letter I is said this way in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone notes that they were named in official messages.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large South Asian country, and in radio spelling it is the word that stands for the letter I.

clue.text: This person, volunteer with upturned collar, kind of European

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves is I
TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: in a down clue upturned means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to collar or nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A volunteer with a turned-up collar strikes a certain continental pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Italy is one particular nationality on the European continent.

clue.text: Makes team tea, possibly? Specific info needed!

definitions.meaning: to detail someone is to assign them a task, such as brewing up for the squad
particular facts or items of information

explanation.surface: Someone making tea for the team demands specific instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: In military usage, to detail is to assign someone to a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: It means assigns to a duty and also particular facts or specifics.

clue.text: Transport pilots in waterway linking delta and sierra

indicators.note: linking says the waterway sits between the two letters, joining them

parts.note: Delta is the radio code word for D
Sierra is the radio code word for S
a river is a natural waterway

explanation.surface: Shipping pilots work on a waterway that connects a delta with a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: People who drive buses, lorries or cabs pilot vehicles, so they steer transport.

clue.text: Beloved newspaper — American, from the South

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read from bottom to top

parts.note: rag is slang for a poor-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper from the American South is fondly regarded.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a term of endearment for a loved one, like honey or darling.

clue.text: Criticised houses neglected at first on a slope

indicators.note: houses means takes in, so the criticism word holds a letter inside it

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of neglected

explanation.surface: Neglected houses, already slammed by inspectors, stand on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tilted or leaning sits at an angle, as though on a slope.

clue.text: Crying out for reconditioned engine to tour Germany

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the rebuilt letters circle the German code
a reconditioned engine is rebuilt, so its letters are reassembled

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A motorist badly needs a rebuilt engine before driving around Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconditioned' turns ENGINE into NEEING, and 'to tour' wraps it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying out for something means badly requiring it, an idiom for wanting.

clue.text: View from Llandudno — I nip out with a backward look

indicators.note: a backward look means the letters are read from right to left
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker at Llandudno, the Welsh seaside town, pops out and glances back at the view.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'Llandudno — I nip out' backwards gives TUOPINIONDUDNALL, which holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a belief or judgement is a synonym for a considered point of view.

clue.text: Amounts of beef and lamb maybe needed with certain chaps in

indicators.note: in places the certain chaps inside the word for beef and lamb

parts.note: beef and lamb are examples of meats
sure means certain
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A butcher's recipe calls for quantities of beef and lamb, with some reliable men brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured quantities of ingredients are amounts, as in a recipe's list.
